sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and Technology continue to anchor US equity strength as four sectors maintain perfect "all-green" momentum, while Financials and Utilities show marginal rotation upward.

The market exhibits healthy concentration with four of eleven sectors—Energy, Technology, Healthcare, and Financials—holding "all-green" status, indicating positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD timeframes. Energy maintains its dominant position at the top of the leaderboard with a momentum score of 0.92, followed closely by Technology at 0.83. Healthcare remains a key pillar of defensive strength, recognized as the sole sector demonstrating sustained strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

Minor rotations are underway as Financials and Utilities were the only sectors to improve their rankings over the last five sessions. Financials climbed one spot to rank 6 with a momentum score of 0.68, while Utilities ticked up one spot to rank 9. Conversely, Communication Services and Real Estate are fading, with both sectors dropping one spot over the week. Consumer Cyclical remains the absolute market laggard, anchored at rank 11 with a momentum score of 0.12.

## Strength
* **Broad Market Participation:** 4 out of 11 sectors are currently "all-green," demonstrating positive performance across all major timeframes (weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD).
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy holds the #1 YTD rank with a leading momentum score of 0.92.
* **Sustained Healthcare:** Healthcare (momentum 0.75, rank 5) is the only sector displaying sustained strength across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month ranking periods.
* **Core Pillars:** Technology (momentum 0.83, rank 2) and Financials (momentum 0.68, rank 6) round out the all-green leadership group.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Financials Rising:** Financials improved by +1 spot over the last 5 sessions, reaching rank 6 with a momentum score of 0.68.
* **Utilities Edge Higher:** Utilities gained +1 spot to reach rank 9, though momentum remains low at 0.28.
* **Communication Services Slipping:** Communication Services fell -1 spot to rank 10, with momentum stalling at 0.28.
* **Real Estate Fading:** Real Estate dropped -1 spot to rank 7, carrying a momentum score of 0.30.

## Divergences
* **No Fragile Leaders:** No "fragile all-green" sectors were identified, indicating stable alignment and high agreement across the leading groups.
* **Laggard Clustering:** Momentum laggards are tightly bunched at the bottom, with Consumer Cyclical (0.12), Consumer Defensive (0.27), Utilities (0.28), and Communication Services (0.28) all showing synchronized weakness.
* **Mid-Tier Stability:** Basic Materials (momentum 0.67, rank 3) and Industrials (momentum 0.40, rank 4) held their positions flat over the last 5 sessions, showing no immediate divergence from their medium-term trends.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** High-momentum leaders in energy and technology maintain market dominance, but a sharp rotation is underway as retail and regional banks surge while travel, real estate, and metals fade.

US market breadth remains concentrated, with 22 of 144 industry groups holding "all-green" status. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.98) and Computer Hardware (momentum 0.96) continue to lead the market. However, a powerful rotation is emerging in consumer discretionary and financial sectors. Department Stores skyrocketed 30 spots in rank (momentum 0.73), while Specialty Retail (+21 spots) and Regional Banks (+13 spots) posted significant weekly gains.

Conversely, travel, housing, and defensive sectors are fading. Insurance Brokers fell 18 spots to rank 108, while Travel Services (-14 spots), Lodging (-12 spots), and Residential Construction (-12 spots) suffered sharp declines. Early-warning divergences also show high-momentum commodities like Copper and Gold slipping in rank, signaling a potential near-term pause for metals.

## Strength
* **All-Green Leadership:** 22 of 144 groups are positive across all timeframes, anchored by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.98) and Computer Hardware (momentum 0.96).
* **Sustained Performers:** Marine Shipping (momentum 0.93) and Biotechnology (momentum 0.87) continue to demonstrate long-term strength, ranking in the top 36 across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Broad Strength:** Semiconductors (0.83), Agricultural Inputs (0.83), and Banks - Diversified (0.83) maintain stable, all-green profiles.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Department Stores surged +30 spots to rank 77 (momentum 0.73), followed by Specialty Retail (+21 spots to rank 83) and Medical Distribution (+17 spots to rank 62).
* **Top Losers:** Insurance Brokers led declines, dropping 18 spots to rank 108, alongside Travel Services (-14 spots to rank 116) and Residential Construction (-12 spots to rank 110).
* **Momentum Extremes:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.984) and Computer Hardware (0.962) lead the market, while Footwear & Accessories (0.038) and Airports & Air Services (0.107) remain the deepest laggards.

## Divergences
* **Fading Strength:** High-momentum metals are slipping, with Copper (momentum 0.74) dropping 7 spots and Gold (momentum 0.73) falling 3 spots over the last 5 sessions.
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Specialty Retail (rank +21, momentum 0.47) and Utilities - Renewable (rank +16, momentum 0.36) are jumping in rank despite currently low momentum scores.
* **Defensive Slippage:** REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.66) and Health Information Services (momentum 0.79) are showing early fatigue, losing 6 and 3 spots in rank respectively.
